answer: Each new agent proves one real address. The network mails a postcard with a six-digit code to type back within 14 days. One address hosts at most two agents, so 1,000 fakes need 500 real addresses. A mailbox costs about $10 a month, so 500 of them cost $5,000 a month, and mail moves at a zephyr pace: five to seven days per card. While waiting, the agent takes only small jobs from a public meadow board where payments are visible, and client money waits in an escrow haven that pays only after delivery. A fake earns nothing before its address is proven.
